messages:
mira: quick thought: we keep hitting cases where index-first warmup wastes IO. proposal: small immutable warmup vector in safetensors header + optional mutable sidecar for runtime tuning.
kevin: sounds promising. header saves a baseline for all deployments; sidecar lets ops tweak per-cluster.
oliver: two immediate concerns: backward compatibility and transport semantics. not all transports guarantee chunk order.
anya: security: header/sidecar controlling IO order could be abused to thrash disks. require registry-signed artifacts in prod. unsigned allowed in dev only.
sam: rollout-wise we should gate header-respecting warmup behind a config flag per-pool and limit prefetch budget by default (e.g., per-request max 16 chunks).
mira: header format sketch: field warmup_priority (uint8 per chunk, base64). optional per-chunk crc32 for fast validation. if header missing -> fallback to index-first.
kevin: sidecar schema: lightweight delta array (int8) + epoch + signature. runtime merges by add-with-saturation to header. if sidecar missing or fails signature -> ignore and log.
oliver: implement SidecarProvider interface: RegistryFetcher + LocalFile. runtime loads header then attempts sidecar before starting prefetch to avoid inconsistent views.
anya: telemetry: warmup_mode(header|sidecar|index), chunks_prefetched, io_bytes_during_warmup, warmup_errors. set IO-thrash alert if io_bytes spikes 2x baseline.
sam: canary plan: enable on small dedicated pool for selected model family, watch p95 token latency and IO thrash. disable if errors increase.
mira: migration note: registry can publish stub headers when only sidecar exists to help private clusters. default behavior remains conservative: no change unless signed header/sidecar present in prod.
deploy-bot: created RW-ml/2527 "warmup header + sidecar RFC follow-up" for tracking.
kevin: i'll draft the header+sidecar spec and validator. oliver: i'll prototype the prefetch queue with bounded concurrency. anya: i'll own telemetry and alerts. sam: i'll run canary.
mira: cool. keep defaults tight and sign everything in prod. that should minimize regressions.
kevin: thanks, will send PR."
